prompt: What really caused the 2008 financial crisis? Tell it as a story starting from the US housing boom, include subprime mortgages, securitization, Lehman Brothers and the government response.

plan.title: What really caused the 2008 financial crisis
plan.description: The story of the 2008 financial crisis, from the US housing boom and subprime mortgages to securitization, the fall of Lehman Brothers and the government response. It shows how a chain of risky decisions turned a housing problem into a global crisis.

beats.narration: A bet on American homes nearly broke the world economy. It began with a housing boom. Prices kept rising, banks lent freely, and subprime mortgages went to borrowers who were unlikely to repay.

clip_queries: for sale sign in front of house

beats.narration: Then came securitization. Banks bundled thousands of mortgages into securities and sold them to investors around the world. Lenders no longer carried the risk, so the risk spread everywhere.

Then housing prices fell. Borrowers defaulted, and those securities lost value. Banks feared each other's losses and stopped lending. In September 2008, Lehman Brothers collapsed, and panic spread across global markets.

Governments stepped in. They rescued banks, cut interest rates and pumped money into the system. It stopped the freefall, but millions lost jobs and homes. Easy credit, hidden risk and weak oversight caused the crisis.
The lesson is simple. When risk is hidden, everyone pays for it. Ask who really holds the risk.

props.text: When risk is hidden, everyone eventually pays for it.
